name: Not X but Y
guidance: Check contrasts that inflate a point without answering a real belief; keep informative contrasts.

name: One-line closers and dramatic fragments
guidance: Look for repeated closers, slogans or fragments that restate a preceding point without adding information.

name: Sayings that sound deep
guidance: Check pseudo-profound framing or aphorisms that substitute weight for a specific claim.

name: Staged run-up before the point
guidance: Check staged openings or announcements of the explanation before an ordinary claim.

name: Arguing with no one
guidance: Check unraised objections and fake alternatives; retain objections that readers actually need answered.

name: Forced triads
guidance: Check whether repeated groups of three add distinct ideas; three necessary items are ordinary.

name: Repeated sentence openings
guidance: Inspect formulaic repeated openings, respecting deliberate human rhythm.

name: Dashes as the universal connector
guidance: Repeated dash constructions are weak alone; punctuation and personal style are not authorship evidence.

name: Stacked qualifiers
guidance: Look for stacked hedges that blur a claim; ordinary uncertainty is appropriate and weak alone.

name: Hyphenated pairs everywhere
guidance: Repeated unnecessary compound hyphens after nouns are weak alone; technical terms may require them.

name: Passive voice and missing subjects
guidance: Repeated missing actors may obscure meaning; useful passive voice is weak alone.

name: Overused AI words
guidance: Look for clusters of stock abstract words such as delve, tapestry, testament, pivotal, showcase; respect literal and technical uses.

name: Inflated significance
guidance: Check grand significance, legacy, pivotal moments and optimistic outlooks without concrete support.

name: Vague connection or association
guidance: Check unnamed relationships that the passage could express specifically; do not invent a missing role.

name: Shallow -ing riders
guidance: Check participial riders that add unsupported interpretation to a fact.

name: Sales language
guidance: Check promotional scenery and praise in prose whose genre calls for plain description.

name: Borrowed authority
guidance: Check unnamed experts or prestige lists that replace the actual supported claim; lack of citations alone is ordinary.

name: Avoiding is, are, and has
guidance: Check showy verb substitutions where simple verbs would express the same supported meaning.

name: Bold as decoration
guidance: Check repeated bold labels and visual decoration without a purpose; consider document conventions.

name: Decorative headings
guidance: Check repeated title-case or decorated headings that add no useful structure.

name: Curly quotation marks
guidance: Editor-created curly quotes are weak alone and must never support an authorship conclusion.

name: Chatbot residue
guidance: Check greetings, praise, offers or closings left in standalone prose; real correspondence has ordinary greetings.

name: Knowledge-limit disclaimers and guesses
guidance: Check model-training disclaimers and unsupported plausible guesses; genuine uncertainty is appropriate.

name: A heading repeated in the first sentence
guidance: Check an opening sentence that merely restates the heading.

name: Writing about the document instead of its subject
guidance: Check redundant descriptions of layout or drafting; source credits, change logs and consequential caveats are useful.

name: Re-explaining what the reader knows
guidance: Assess only when conversation or audience context is present; do not guess what a reader knows.
